cgroup: Original 64 GiB / swap 0 cgroup, birth/PIDFD-bound original processes, E16-31, 1GiB component own aggregate RSS, 64MiB output and 25GiB host reserve; no performance qualification of shared cgroup
corrections: Console numeric floating carriers contain both IEEE bits and value=decimal. The old DAP Source variables parser admitted bits-only carriers and rejected the complete real list.
New detached float parser bounds decimal grammar and checks a single exact ties-to-even rounding agrees with copied bits, including signed zero, extrema, subnormals and infinity.
Decimal.copy_abs() preserves all admitted decimal digits instead of rounding at the default arithmetic context before exact ratio conversion.
NaN decimal text conveys class only. Its sign and payload come from actual raw IEEE bits, never inferred from text.
Direct named source-stop float leaves expose their copied value and producer type. Legacy bits-only replies remain opaque.
Actual minus-zero and special roots sometimes use object: type=float/double. Bounded direct copied primitive roots now expose scalar display; compound root packets keep their opaque display.

Clang21/lld21 default debug string merging produced a DWARF5 C++ string-offset verifier failure despite valid Wasm. Re-linking genuine compiler objects with lld -O0 yields independently verified debug sections, without rewriting Wasm.
limitations: The new floating live matrix is C/C++/Objective-C/Objective-C++ only, wasm32/64, DWARF4/5, O0/O1; OC fixtures exercise primitive frontend metadata and do not inherit ObjC runtime/object semantics.
Rust/TinyGo/Zig controls qualify their existing finite expression/object routes, not every new floating parameter ABI.
Standard Go and AssemblyScript floating routes, optimized full language semantics, all native debugger features and full cross-architecture VM/JIT/DAP remain unqualified.
Only the frozen R51 full products and their historical LLVM23 provider are used; current local peer changes and latest ROS provider are preserved outside this cut.
No language metadata, scalar display, NaN label, address, evaluateName or variablesReference is promoted to guest read/write, expansion or VM-debugging authority.
